rearrange_string_k_distance_apart.brute:
if k <= 1: return s
counts = dict letter -> count, out = []
place():   (backtracking, one slot at a time)
    if size of out == size of s: return true
    recent = set of the last k - 1 letters placed
    for each letter ch in sorted order:
        if counts[ch] > 0 and ch not in recent:
            counts[ch] = counts[ch] - 1, append ch to out
            if place(): return true
            undo: pop ch from out, counts[ch] = counts[ch] + 1
    return false
return out joined if place() succeeds else ""
rearrange_string_k_distance_apart.optimal:
if k <= 1: return s
counts = dict letter -> count
heap = max-heap of (count, letter)
cooldown = queue of (count, letter) waiting out k slots, out = []
repeat n times:
    if heap is empty: return ""   (every letter is still cooling down: impossible)
    pop the most frequent (count, ch), append ch to out
    append (count - 1, ch) to the back of cooldown
    if size of cooldown == k:
        pop the front; if it still has copies left push it back onto the heap
return out joined

merge_k_sorted_lists.brute:
values = []
for each list head:
    walk the list appending every value to values
sort values   (ignores that each list is already sorted)
build and return a new linked list from values
merge_k_sorted_lists.optimal:
heads = the current front node of each list
heap = min-heap of (value, list index) for every non-empty head
dummy = new node, tail = dummy
while heap is not empty:
    pop the smallest (value, i)   (the globally smallest remaining node)
    node = heads[i], tail.next = node, tail = node
    heads[i] = node.next
    if heads[i] exists: push (heads[i].value, i)
return dummy.next

kth_smallest_prime_fraction.brute:
fractions = []
for each i, for each j after i:
    append (arr[i] / arr[j], arr[i], arr[j]) to fractions
sort fractions by value   (sorts fractions that can never be among the first k)
return [numerator, denominator] of fractions[k - 1]
kth_smallest_prime_fraction.optimal:
heap = min-heap of (arr[i] / arr[n - 1], i, n - 1) for each i < n - 1   (each row's smallest)
repeat k - 1 times:
    pop the smallest (value, i, j)
    if j - 1 > i: push (arr[i] / arr[j - 1], i, j - 1)   (row i's next fraction)
(value, i, j) = top of heap
return [arr[i], arr[j]]

smallest_range_covering_elements_from_k_.optimal:
heap = min-heap of (value, list index, position) with the first element of each list
current_max = largest of those first elements
best = [top of heap, current_max]
repeat forever:
    pop the smallest (value, i, j)   (the low end of the range)
    if current_max - value < width of best: best = [value, current_max]
    if j + 1 == size of list i: return best   (list i is exhausted: no later range covers it)
    next_value = lists[i][j + 1]
    push (next_value, i, j + 1)
    current_max = max(current_max, next_value)

find_median_from_data_stream.brute:
init:
    nums = []
add_num(num):
    append num to nums
find_median:
    ordered = sorted nums, n = size of ordered   (re-sorts everything on every query)
    if n is odd: return ordered[n / 2]
    return (ordered[n / 2 - 1] + ordered[n / 2]) / 2
find_median_from_data_stream.optimal:
init:
    small = max-heap (lower half), large = min-heap (upper half)
add_num(num):
    push num into small
    move the largest of small into large   (keeps every small <= every large)
    if size of large > size of small: move the smallest of large back into small
find_median:
    if size of small > size of large: return the top of small
    return (top of small + top of large) / 2

ipo.brute:
done = array of false values
repeat k times:
    best = -1
    for each project j:
        if done[j] or capital[j] > w: skip it
        if best < 0 or profits[j] > profits[best]: best = j
    if best < 0: break   (nothing affordable now, and w will not grow)
    done[best] = true
    w = w + profits[best]
return w
ipo.optimal:
projects = (capital, profit) pairs sorted by capital
unlocked = max-heap of profits, i = 0
repeat k times:
    while i < n and projects[i].capital <= w:   (w only grows, so i only moves right)
        push projects[i].profit, i = i + 1
    if unlocked is empty: break
    w = w + pop the largest profit
return w

minimum_number_of_refueling_stops.optimal:
passed = max-heap of gas amounts at stations driven past
fuel = start_fuel, stops = 0
for each (position, gas) in stations followed by (target, 0):
    while fuel < position:   (cannot reach it yet: refuel retroactively at the best station passed)
        if passed is empty: return -1
        fuel = fuel + pop the largest gas
        stops = stops + 1
    push gas
return stops

course_schedule_iii.optimal:
ordered = (deadline, duration) pairs sorted by deadline
taken = max-heap of durations
time = 0
for each (deadline, duration) in ordered:
    push duration, time = time + duration
    if time > deadline:
        longest = pop the largest duration   (drop the longest course: frees the most time)
        time = time - longest
return size of taken

maximum_performance_of_a_team.brute:
best = 0
for each size from 1 to k:
    for each team of that size:
        total_speed = sum of the team's speeds
        min_efficiency = smallest efficiency in the team
        best = max(best, total_speed * min_efficiency)
return best mod 1e9 + 7
maximum_performance_of_a_team.optimal:
engineers = (efficiency, speed) pairs sorted by efficiency descending
fastest = min-heap of speeds, total_speed = 0, best = 0
for each (efficiency, speed) in engineers:
    push speed, total_speed = total_speed + speed
    if size of fastest > k: total_speed = total_speed - pop the smallest speed
    best = max(best, total_speed * efficiency)   (this engineer is the team's bottleneck)
return best mod 1e9 + 7

minimize_deviation_in_array.brute:
ladder(x): odd x -> [x, 2x]; even x -> x, x / 2, x / 4, ... down to its odd core
ladders = ladder(x) for each x in nums
best = none
for each choice of one rung per ladder:
    deviation = max of choice - min of choice
    if best is none or deviation < best: best = deviation
return best
minimize_deviation_in_array.optimal:
heap = max-heap of each number, doubled once if odd   (the top of every ladder)
low = smallest value in the heap
best = none
repeat forever:
    high = pop the top of heap
    if best is none or high - low < best: best = high - low
    if high is odd: return best   (the maximum can no longer shrink)
    push high / 2
    low = min(low, high / 2)

meeting_rooms_iii.optimal:
sort meetings by start
free = min-heap of room numbers 0..n - 1
busy = min-heap of (end time, room), count = array of n zeros
for each (start, end):
    while busy is not empty and the earliest end <= start: move that room to free
    if free is not empty: room = pop the lowest room number
    else:
        (earliest_end, room) = pop the earliest finishing room   (ties: lowest number)
        end = earliest_end + (end - start)
    push (end, room) into busy
    count[room] = count[room] + 1
return the index of the largest count

the_skyline_problem.brute:
tallest_at(x): the tallest height among buildings with left <= x < right, or 0
edges = sorted distinct left and right values
out = [], previous = 0
for each x in edges:   (the outline can only change at an edge)
    height = tallest_at(x)
    if height != previous:
        append [x, height] to out
        previous = height
return out

trapping_rain_water_ii.brute:
level[r][c] = height on the border, infinity inside   (water level over each cell)
changed = true
while changed:
    changed = false
    for each inner cell (r, c):
        lowest_neighbour = min level among the 4 neighbours
        new_level = max(height_map[r][c], lowest_neighbour)
        if new_level < level[r][c]: level[r][c] = new_level, changed = true
return sum of level[r][c] - height_map[r][c] over all cells
trapping_rain_water_ii.optimal:
seen = grid of false, frontier = min-heap of (level, r, c)
for each border cell: mark seen, push (height, r, c)
water = 0
while frontier is not empty:
    pop the lowest (level, r, c)   (water leaks out over the lowest wall first)
    for each 4-neighbour (nr, nc) inside the grid and not seen:
        mark seen
        height = height_map[nr][nc]
        water = water + max(0, level - height)
        push (max(level, height), nr, nc)
return water
